about.title: Founded in 1988, and still building on the same Gulf Coast.
text: In 1988, Larry Hogan and Dudley Masterson founded H&M Design, an industrial engineering and design firm in La Porte, TX. Construction was added to the service lines in 2001, which began the growth into full service solutions for clients, and the team moved to its current, larger Pasadena facility in 2009.

H&M Design was re-branded to H+M Industrial EPC in 2013 to communicate the full list of offerings to clients in the region. Brandon Hogan, P.E. was named President and CEO in 2017, and the Woodlands, TX office opened in 2019. The fabrication shop expansion completed in Q1 of 2020 tripled the previous production capacity.

Our vision is to be the preferred partner for EPC projects in the Energy and Chemicals industries, providing trust, expertise and efficiency. We provide maximum value to clients by hiring and retaining the best employees, developing future talent, and encouraging a culture of responsibility and accountability.

faqs.q: What do your detailed design engineering services cover?
faqs.a: Comprehensive engineering and design services address all project areas, from conception to implementation.

faqs.q: What types of engineering and design services do you offer?
faqs.a: Wide-ranging engineering and design services, including feasibility studies, front-end engineering and design (FEED), detailed design, and construction support services.

faqs.q: How are 3D models and simulation technologies used?
faqs.a: 3D models and simulations, using advanced technology and software tools, help customers visualize capital projects and identify possible concerns before construction begins.

faqs.q: What is the benefit of a long-term maintenance contract?
faqs.a: A long-term maintenance contract improves continuity and performance by stabilizing the workforce and strengthening accountability. Facilities benefit from stable crews familiar with the site, dedicated supervision, and clearer ownership of outcomes across safety, quality, and productivity.

faqs.q: Why is supervised craft important for plant maintenance?
faqs.a: Supervised craft is important because daily work quality, safety performance, and productivity are driven by direct field leadership. A supervised model creates clearer accountability at the point of execution and reduces the variability that comes from fragmented oversight and labor-only contractor structures.

faqs.q: How do your services improve efficiency and cost management?
faqs.a: Our approach is centered on improving project efficiency and cost-effectiveness through strategic planning, advanced technologies, and experienced project execution.

faqs.q: How do you reduce contractor churn in industrial facilities?
faqs.a: H+M reduces contractor churn by employing a stable workforce model supported by dedicated H+M on-site supervision. Because we own the workforce and the on-site leadership, facilities avoid the rotating crew problem that creates repeated resets in performance and safety consistency.

Outside Battery Limits cooling-loop EPC refers to the piping, structural steel, and cooling equipment installation that connect data center cooling systems outside the data hall across a campus. It typically includes chilled water and condenser water systems serving one or multiple buildings or phases.

faqs.q: When should a data center cooling contractor be engaged?
faqs.a: Early involvement during preconstruction allows cooling-loop execution strategy, fabrication planning, structural coordination, and labor strategy alignment with overall campus phasing and schedule milestones.

faqs.q: How is industrial piping for data centers different from commercial HVAC piping?
faqs.a: Industrial piping for data centers involves larger diameters, heavier materials, greater structural integration, and more complex sequencing across multi-building campuses than interior commercial HVAC systems. It requires industrial-grade supervision and execution depth to maintain productivity and schedule performance.

faqs.q: Can H+M handle cooling infrastructure for multi-phase hyperscale campuses?
faqs.a: Yes. Our OSBL cooling-loop EPC model is structured specifically for phased campus delivery, with integrated engineering, fabrication and construction teams engaged early to align cooling-loop sequencing with staggered building delivery, shared infrastructure tie-ins and expansion allowances for future phases.

Job Safety Analysis is the second line of defence, and crews can stop the job at any point.
